content: 1. Ethinyl estradiol should be initiated at the lowest possible dose and increased only if necessary, up to a maximum of 1 mg/5 mcg. It is not recommended for premenarcheal individuals. 2. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Co-administration of fezolinetant with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors, including ethiny estradiol, increases fezolinetant AUC and peak plasma concentration. This is contraindicated. 4. Ethinyl estradiol, when co-administered with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir, can lead to significant ALT elevations (>5x ULN, including some >20x ULN). Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before initiating these hepatitis C combination drugs and restarted approximately 2 weeks after completing the regimen. 5. Co-administration of tranexamic acid and ethinyl estradiol increases the risk of thrombosis due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Acitretin decreases the effects of norethindrone acetate through an unknown mechanism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 8. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Anastrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 9. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect. 10. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 11. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding may occur. Nonhormonal contraception is advised. Belzutifan may cause fetal harm based on animal studies. 12. Atazanavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 13. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. Brigatinib may cause fetal harm. 14. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 15. Calaspargase pegol may indirectly interact with oral contraceptives, making concomitant use not recommended. Non-oral contraceptive methods should be used for females of childbearing potential. 16. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable in this scenario, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 17. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 18. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 19. Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 20. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 21. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of elagolix through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogen-containing contraceptives are expected to reduce elagolix efficacy. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended during treatment and for 1 week after discontinuation. 22. Elvitegravir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 23. Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative therapies should be considered. 24. Encorafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended during treatment and for 2 weeks after the final dose. Encorafenib may cause fetal harm. 25. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of enoxaparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. 26. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic enzymes CYP3A4 and CYP2E1 metabolism. Co-administration may increase the risk of adverse effects, and alternative drugs should be considered. 27. Fosamprenavir may alter hormone levels and decrease amprenavir AUC when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 28. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 29. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 30. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of heparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. 31. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 32. Indinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 33. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative therapies should be considered. 34. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 35. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP substrates. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 36. Lesinurad decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 37. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of letrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Letrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 38. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative therapies should be considered. 39. Lopinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended.
